notes: Animation names and curve metadata are decoded directly from M_FGT1.BIN.
Ryo move animations are resolved through executable function 0x0c1b1dd4 and the global MOTION.BIN registry, not inferred from M_FGT1 names.

The global MOTION.BIN sequence table's second word identifies an action-metadata record. Opcode 0x02 at metadata +0x0c supplies three native phase-frame halfwords; 44 canonical primary motions expose that record directly.

MOTION/M_FGT1 action-metadata records with the native 04 05 marker carry exact AB76/AB77 DTPK group, track, and animation-frame sound cues; these mappings are extracted structurally rather than assigned by audition.
Canonical move names and English descriptions are extracted from the captured original game RAM.
All 51 moves are joined to their native seven-byte compact command records and displayed WAZA.FON glyph strings.
Opcode 4 is the running/L-trigger modifier and opcode 6 is the guard/Y button; the two display-only positional glyphs distinguish side and rear throws.
Throw victim clips are joined to complete global MOTION.BIN NGR/NAGERARE counterparts by the native NGS/NAGE naming groups; battle-controller call-site confirmation remains pending.
Arm Break Fire's SP2 and SP3 actor requests are confirmed at EN_RYOU bytecode offsets 0x0c14 and 0x0c48; matching victim clips are joined by their exact SP2/SP3 sequence families.
Tornado Kick is represented by its first-kick NIREN1_TOP entry and the catalogue-primary NIREN1_TOP_MK continuation; EN_RYOU also requests the NIREN2_TOP alternate at bytecode offset 0x075c.
Pit Blow's KONGO_TYUKEN_C_MID continuation is requested by EN_RYOU at bytecode offset 0x0884; B and Y_B alternates occur at 0x01f8 and 0x0200.
Damage, hit windows, animation selection, transitions, and AI meanings remain unverified until their native tables and code paths are decoded.

canonicalMoves.name: Tiger Knuckle
canonicalMoves.description: The Tiger Knuckle is a punch aimed at the jinchu, a pressure point located between the nose and mouth

canonicalMoves.name: Elbow Slam
canonicalMoves.description: This move delivers a downward rotating blow from the forearm, aimed at the opponent's collarbone

canonicalMoves.name: Twist Knuckle
canonicalMoves.description: Unlike the Elbow Slam, this blow is thrown horizontally in a sweeping hook

canonicalMoves.name: Elbow Assault
canonicalMoves.description: The Elbow Assault targets the center of the opponent's body with a full-body rush

canonicalMoves.name: Upper Knuckle
canonicalMoves.description: A move where the practitioner momentarily lowers, then raises their body while swinging to strike the opponent in the jaw

canonicalMoves.name: Sleeve Strike
canonicalMoves.description: This move involves taking one step forward with the rear leg and punching at a mid-level target with the fist

canonicalMoves.name: Rain Thrust
canonicalMoves.description: The Rain Thrust is a straight punch aimed at a pressure point on the right side of the opponent's neck

canonicalMoves.name: Big Wheel
canonicalMoves.description: The Big Wheel is a powerful variation of the Elbow Slam. Aimed at the opponent's collarbone, it features a diagonal blow struck once the practitioner closes in

canonicalMoves.name: TwinHandWaves
canonicalMoves.description: This move involves advancing a step forward and striking the opponent's chest and jaw with the palm and entire forearm. The impact creates a shockwave that affects the opponent's internal organs

canonicalMoves.name: Backfist Willow
canonicalMoves.description: This is a surprise attack with a spinning backfist. The spinning motion increases the power of the blow

canonicalMoves.name: AvalancheLance
canonicalMoves.description: This move strikes the pit of the opponent's stomach with an elbow bent at an acute angle, similar to a lance thrust. Experts can do this move while spinning, to evade attacks

canonicalMoves.name: KatanaMistSlash
canonicalMoves.description: The practitioner advances one step with the forward leg and delivers a slashing blow to the opponent's side with the side of the palm

canonicalMoves.name: Mistral Flash
canonicalMoves.description: A move which utilizes the running speed of the practitioner to delivera diagonal cutting blow to the area between the shoulder and the nape of the neck

canonicalMoves.name: Pit Blow
canonicalMoves.description: This double punch begins with a step forward and a mid-level strike with the leading fist, followed by a second punch to the same target with the other hand. Masters of this move can add an elbow strike

canonicalMoves.name: Double Blow
canonicalMoves.description: The practitioner firmly places one palm forward on the enemy's body, steels and slams the palm of the free hand into the back of the other hand in a devastating blow

canonicalMoves.name: Swallow Flip
canonicalMoves.description: This advanced move from the Yang Qing Style involves deflecting the opponent's attack, and kicking the opponent's legs at the same time. It is a closely kept secret, and not easily mastered

canonicalMoves.name: Rising Flash
canonicalMoves.description: After lowering their body momentarily, the practitioner then springs upward to deliver a blow to the opponent's chin

canonicalMoves.name: Twin Blades
canonicalMoves.description: The practitioner lands a chop to the opponent's neck using the sides of the open hands. When this technique is mastered, the practitioner can repeat the attack after the initial strike

canonicalMoves.name: Stab Armor
canonicalMoves.description: Iwao Hazuki learned this move in China. The practitioner strikes a penetrating blow with the palms using power from a twist of the back. Experts can make the blow evenmore powerful by stepping in deeper

canonicalMoves.name: Crescent Kick
canonicalMoves.description: The Crescent Kick is unleashed like an upward sword-stroke, aimed at the opponent's head

canonicalMoves.name: Trample Kick
canonicalMoves.description: This move is similar to a so-called front kick, but is delivered using the entire underside of the foot in a stamping action while targeting the vital organs in the torso

canonicalMoves.name: SideReaperKick
canonicalMoves.description: This is a low, decisive kick aimed at the outside of the opponent's knee

canonicalMoves.name: AgainstCascade
canonicalMoves.description: In this flying knee move, the practitioner leaps upward to kick while restraining the opponent with both hands. Masters of this move can increase its destructive power

canonicalMoves.name: Surplice Slash
canonicalMoves.description: This back roundhouse kick strikes in a downward motion diagonally across the opponent's body. The path of the kick resembles the surplice worn by Buddhist monks

canonicalMoves.name: Thunder Kick
canonicalMoves.description: This kick begins as a high outside spin kick, but ends as a heel drop. The path of the kick is compact, and those who master the move can follow a middle kick with this technique

canonicalMoves.name: HoldAgainstLeg
canonicalMoves.description: This move involves using the power of the forward leg to deliver a low to mid-level kick to the opponent

canonicalMoves.name: Brutal Tiger
canonicalMoves.description: This is a high-speed reverse roundhouse kick. Those who have not yet mastered the move usually find themselves off balance when they miss, but experts can recover with ease

canonicalMoves.name: Dark Moon
canonicalMoves.description: A kick delivered while flipping forward in mid-air, this is one of the more unusual moves in the Hazuki style. Experts leave no openings for an attack after the execution of this move

canonicalMoves.name: Cyclone Kick
canonicalMoves.description: This flying back roundhouse kick is powerful, due to the jump and rotation, but is also easy to dodge.Masters of the move can jump higher to kick

canonicalMoves.name: Windmill
canonicalMoves.description: A flying back kick, this powerful move aims a diagonally slicing kick at the base of the opponent's neck

canonicalMoves.name: Swallow Dive
canonicalMoves.description: This move from the Yang Qing Style is reminiscent of Taekwondo. The initial kick is a feint, and after the opponent is lured in, the practitioner intercepts with the heel drop

canonicalMoves.name: Tornado Kick
canonicalMoves.description: A daring move which uses the spinning momentum from the first spin kick to spin again and deliver a powerful second kick

canonicalMoves.name: Nothing Skill
canonicalMoves.description: Nothing Skill Information

canonicalMoves.name: Crawl Cyclone
canonicalMoves.description: With this move the practitioner Crouches and spins around rapidly on the pivot leg while using the other leg to sweep out the opponent's legs

canonicalMoves.name: Mud Spider
canonicalMoves.description: With this move, the practitioner slides toward the opponent, and kicks upward with the leg, aiming for the abdomen. Experts can also aim for the jaw

canonicalMoves.name: TwinSwallowLeap
canonicalMoves.description: A simple flying kick, but in the hands of an expert, a heel drop can be added after landing from the first kick

canonicalMoves.name: Shadow Reaper
canonicalMoves.description: While running, the practitioner suddenly slides forward along the ground to sweep the feet out from under the opponent. Experts can twist to make the attack stronger

canonicalMoves.name: Overthrow
canonicalMoves.description: With this move, the practitioner takes the opponent's arm and lowers the body while grabbing the opponent's collar, lifting the opponent over the back and throwing

canonicalMoves.name: Sweep Throw
canonicalMoves.description: This throw move involves quickly turning and pulling the opponent's collar, then using the leg to sweep the opponent's inner thigh upwards to throw. In Judo, this move is called |uchimata+

canonicalMoves.name: Vortex Throw
canonicalMoves.description: In this so-called sacrifice throw, similar to the Judo technique of the same name, in which the practitioner falls backward to throw the opponent overhead to the rear

canonicalMoves.name: Mist Reaper
canonicalMoves.description: With this move the practitioner grabs the opponent's neck and pulls forward and down while reaping the legs back and up, effectively applying power in the opposite directions to the upper and lower body

canonicalMoves.name: Demon Drop
canonicalMoves.description: The practitioner uses an armlock to throw the opponent while flipping forward in mid-air during the throw to land on top of the opponent

canonicalMoves.name: Shoulder Buster
canonicalMoves.description: As the opponent attempts a strike, the practitioner grasps the arm and executes an armlock to pin. A common technique in older styles of jujitsu, execution of this move varies from style to style

canonicalMoves.name: Tengu Drop
canonicalMoves.description: This dynamic move involves lowering the body to grasp the opponent's leg, lifting the opponent onto their shoulders and then dropping them headfirst by toppling over sideways

canonicalMoves.name: DarksideHazuki
canonicalMoves.description: This move involves closing in on the opponent's side and throwing down while turning 180 degrees. This technique is one of the major Hazuki throws, and dates back to the early days of the style

canonicalMoves.name: BackTwistDrop
canonicalMoves.description: Similar to the back drop move used in pro wrestling, it has been adapted to make it more difficult to defend against. The throw is executed with a twist toward the rear

canonicalMoves.name: Shadow Step
canonicalMoves.description: This move involving the evasion of an opponent's attack while moving behind to attack from the blind spot

canonicalMoves.name: Arm Break Fire
canonicalMoves.description: A complex move that damages the opponent's arms in multiple areas simultaneously. When executed by one who has mastered the technique, the opponent is left wondering what happened to them

canonicalMoves.name: Tiger Storm
canonicalMoves.description: The practitioner momentarily crouches to gather strength before aggressively lunging into the opponent. Experts can add a shoulder strike after the initial impact

canonicalMoves.name: Shadow Blade
canonicalMoves.description: This move is an extension of the Shadow Step. After slipping into the opponent's blind spot, the practitioner strikes the back of the neck

canonicalMoves.name: Cross Charge
canonicalMoves.description: This is a combined defensive and offensive move where the practitioner evades an opponent's attack diagonally, then moves in for an elbow strike
